title: Novel relationship annotation
description: Annotation of romantic, erotic, sexual, conjugal, desirous, or historically coded relations in late nineteenth- and early twentieth-century novels. Version 2: relation_type redefined (queer, mixed_gender), six new closed fields (structure, status, reciprocity, exclusivity, adultery, explicitness_in_plot), and structured evidence with verbatim quotations.

relation_id.description: Identifier of the relation within this novel: R1, R2, R3, and so on, ordered by narrative importance.

characters.description: Names or designations of the participants. Use the fullest form the text provides; a collective participant may be named as a group.

relation_type.description: Gender configuration of the participants, not the certainty that the relation is romantic or sexual. female_male: one character identified as female and one identified as male. female_female: two characters identified as female. male_male: two characters identified as male. mixed_gender: relation mixing several gender patterns. unknown_gender: relation is present, but the gender of one or more participants cannot be reliably determined from the text. queer: relation involving one or more gender non-conforming person(s), for instance characters that could be described as intersex, genderfluid, non-binary, or agender, or whose sex or gender status the text presents as unstable. unclear: relation candidate is present, but its relational configuration cannot be reliably determined.

structure.description: Number and shape of the participants. dyadic: relation between two people. triangular: relation between three people. group_or_milieu: mutual relationship between more than three people. hierarchy_group: relationship within a group centered around a particular character. unclear: the shape of the relation cannot be determined.

status.description: Nature of the bond. married: married couple. engaged: engaged couple. romantic_relationship: a relationship involving romantic feelings. physical_relationship: a physical (sexual) relationship that does not seem to involve, or is not supposed to involve, romantic feelings. ambiguous_friendship: a relationship officially presented as a platonic friendship, but in which words, gestures and/or actions suggest that at least one of the two parties is attracted to the other. seduction: a relationship in which at least one of the parties is attracted to the other and sets out to seduce them. unclear: not enough evidence to assess whether the relationship involves romantic feelings, physical relations, or only seduction.

reciprocity.description: Balance of commitment between the participants. one_sided: only one of the two characters is attracted to or interested in engaging in a relationship with the other. reciprocal: both characters are generally equally committed to one another; exceptions may occur in particular situations, such as a passing argument. asymmetrical: despite a shared basis of reciprocity, for instance in an established relationship, one of the characters is more committed than the other or views the relationship differently. unclear: the balance of commitment cannot be determined.

exclusivity.description: Rules of exclusivity the relation operates under. exclusive: the characters are emotionally and physically exclusive to one another and do not allow themselves any romantic or sexual relationship with anyone else. emotionally_exclusive: the characters allow themselves physical relationships with other people as long as they do not develop romantic feelings for them. primary_relationship: both partners are free to have other relationships, but this one holds particular importance or takes centre stage. secondary_relationship: one or more of the characters involved are in several relationships, and this one is not the most important. polyamory: each character is free to have, or actively pursues, several romantic and/or sexual relationships, and none takes priority over the others. adultery: an adulterous relationship, that is, one in which at least one of the partners is cheating on their official partner by engaging in it. uncommitted: neither party has made any promise regarding exclusivity. unclear: not enough evidence to assess whether the relationship is exclusive.

adultery.description: Whether the rules recorded in exclusivity, or those of an outside partner, are broken. loyal: both parties respect the rules regarding exclusivity. adultery_one: one of the parties disrespects the rules regarding exclusivity. adultery_both: both parties disrespect the rules regarding exclusivity. external_adultery: by engaging in this relationship, at least one of the parties is cheating on another partner; use together with exclusivity = adultery. none: the issue of adultery does not arise in this context, as with one-sided romantic pursuits or casual relationships. unclear: not enough evidence provided.

explicitness.description: How directly the narration represents the relation. explicit: the text names, stages, or directly confesses love, desire, sex, marriage, adultery, kisses, or erotic attachment. coded: the relation is suggested through euphemism, fascination, jealousy, intense intimacy, repeated symbolic language, or historical codes. rumor: the relation exists mainly as gossip, scandal, accusation, reputation, blackmail, or public suspicion. weak_inference: a queer or romantic reading is possible but fragile; use sparingly. unclear: the degree of explicitness cannot be determined.

explicitness_in_plot.description: How openly the relation is known among the characters, independently of how the narration represents it. explicit: a relationship known to all the characters. explicit_except: a relationship that is generally known, but kept hidden from certain specific characters in the plot. hidden_except: a relationship that is generally kept secret, but which is known to one or several specific characters in the plot. hidden: a relationship kept secret from everyone except the characters involved in it. unclear: the diegetic openness of the relation cannot be determined.

centrality.description: Narrative weight of the relation. main: central to the novel, the protagonist's trajectory, or the main plot. secondary: an important subplot, or affects the main characters, but is not the main relation. episode: a brief adventure, temptation, encounter, confession, memory, or scene. milieu: a background element of a social world such as a salon, brothel, convent, boarding school, decadent circle, or theater. unclear: centrality cannot be determined.

framing.description: Dominant evaluative framing. Choose one only; explain a plausible secondary framing in comment. positive: presented as love, solidarity, attachment, care, mutual recognition, or a livable bond. neutral_ambivalent: neither clearly condemned nor clearly valorized, or the judgment remains mixed. eroticized_exoticized: framed as spectacle, sensual curiosity, voyeuristic scene, exotic setting, or erotic ornament. decadent_sublime: morbid, painful, sacrificial, sacred, aestheticized, feverish, cruel, or sublime, without being reducible to moral condemnation or medical pathology. redemptive_spiritualized: framed as salvation, spiritual refuge, healing, purification, compassion, or quasi-religious rescue. moralized_pathologized: associated with vice, sin, degeneration, illness, hysteria, perversion, crime, or moral decline. comic_caricatural: framed as ridiculous, grotesque, satirical, or comic. predatory_or_corrupting: framed as emprise, manipulation, initiation into vice, corruption, coercion, or predation. unclear: the dominant framing cannot be determined.

outcome.description: Narrative resolution of the relation. stable_or_open: the relation continues, remains possible, or is not narratively destroyed. open_contested: the ending is suspended, disputed, reopened, or undecidable; rival relations or unresolved attachments remain active. return_to_norm: return to marriage, heterosexuality, family order, social respectability, or normative domesticity. separation_erasure: the relation ends through separation, disappearance, forgetting, narrative marginalization, or erasure. social_disgrace: the relation leads to scandal, reputational ruin, exclusion, blackmail, or public shame. illness_madness_decline: the relation is followed by illness, madness, physical decline, moral degradation, or psychological collapse. fatal_ending: the relation is followed by a fatal narrative resolution affecting one or more central characters. unclear: the outcome cannot be determined.

evidence.description: One to ten pieces of evidence supporting the closed labels. Give the verbatim passage in quote whenever a specific line or short passage carries a label; most items should have one. Use description alone when the evidence is a pattern spread across the novel rather than a quotable line.

quote.description: Verbatim passage copied from the novel, reproduced exactly, without normalizing spelling, accents, or punctuation. Omit when no single passage carries the point.

locator.description: Where the passage is found: chapter, part, section, or page, if determinable from the text. Omit when unknown; do not invent one.

description.description: What this evidence shows and which label it supports. When quote is omitted, this carries the whole piece of evidence as a paraphrase.

confidence.description: Security of the annotation. high: several convergent textual cues, little doubt. medium: plausible and supported, but some interpretive ambiguity remains. low: fragile, useful for review but not for conservative statistics. exclude: the candidate should probably not be counted as an annotated relationship.

comment.description: Brief free-text justification: dominant versus secondary readings, why a difficult label was chosen, and anything that makes the annotation auditable.
